name: Dart G
summary: 1930s two-seat low-wing sport plane from Al Mooney's Dart Aircraft Company, the ancestor of the Culver Cadet. Fixed gear and a tailwheel, usually powered by a small radial.

wings: Low cantilever wing with no struts
engines: Small five-cylinder radial in a neat cowl (flat-four on the GC)
fuselage: Compact two-seat fuselage with clean lines
Fixed main gear with a tailwheel

tellTales: Small prewar low-wing two-seater with a radial nose
No struts and fixed tailwheel gear on a very clean airframe
Compact fuselage with small, tidy tail surfaces

confusedWith.howToTell: The Cadet has a flat-four, a smoother metal fuselage and retractable main gear; the Dart has a radial nose and fixed gear.
The Monocoupe is a high-wing; the Dart is a low-wing.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
